review_fix_inputs.findings_section:
FINDINGS

- `src/ui.rs:695-697`, `src/ui.rs:938-942`, `src/ui.rs:1047-1065`: right-pane visual selection ignores wrapped display rows. The pane renders with `Paragraph::wrap`, but selection/copy treats each newline as one row and paints `range.row` directly into the buffer. Long agent lines can visibly wrap across multiple rows, while visual highlight/cursor movement/copy operate on the unwrapped logical line, so selected text can differ from what is highlighted. The new tests only cover short unwrapped lines.

- `src/terminal_app.rs:545-547`, `src/terminal_app.rs:799-811`; same harness path at `src/ui_harness.rs:181-183`, `src/ui_harness.rs:423-433`: `/` is intercepted before visual-mode keys reach `TerminalUi::handle_visual_key`. In visual mode over an agent chat, `mode == Command` and `selected_agent().is_some()`, so pressing `/` clears the visual selection via `activate_agent_chat` and inserts `/` into the chat buffer instead of preserving/handling the active visual selection.

FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:430-471`, `src/ui.rs:781-800`: visual-mode arrow movement does not work in the real terminal byte path. `handle_bytes` feeds escape sequences byte by byte, and because visual mode still reports `UiMode::Command`, the leading `Esc` is dispatched immediately and clears `visual_selection` before `\x1b[D`/`\x1b[A` is decoded into `UiKey::Left`/`Up`. The decoded arrow then routes as normal command-mode input instead of moving the visual cursor. The harness tests miss this because `UiHarness::handle_bytes` pre-parses complete escape sequences before bytewise handling.

FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:822-825`, `src/terminal_app.rs:430-451`, `src/cli.rs:1019-1028`: a lone `Esc` no longer exits visual mode in the interactive terminal path. The new visual-mode branch in `defer_escape_key` stores the escape as pending, but `handle_terminal_bytes` does not flush it after a normal nonzero read; the CLI only calls `finish_pending_terminal_input` on `read == 0`. The added tests use `handle_bytes`, which flushes pending input, so they miss the actual interactive path where pressing `Esc` by itself leaves the visual selection active until another key arrives.

FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:430-439`, `src/terminal_app.rs:831-836`: visual-mode arrow sequences still break if the terminal read splits `Esc` from the rest of the sequence. `handle_terminal_bytes(b"\x1b")` now immediately flushes the pending visual `Esc` and exits visual mode, so a later `handle_terminal_bytes(b"[C")` is processed as normal command text instead of reaching `UiKey::Right`. The new tests only cover `handle_terminal_bytes(b"\x1b[C")` in one chunk, but the CLI consumes arbitrary `stdin.read` chunks at `src/cli.rs:1019-1028`.

FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:563`, `src/terminal_app.rs:569`, `src/terminal_app.rs:1078`, and the mirrored harness path at `src/ui_harness.rs:184`, `src/ui_harness.rs:187`, `src/ui_harness.rs:587`: byte `22` is now parsed as `Char('\u{16}')` for Ctrl-V, but prompt/insert-mode `Char(ch)` arms run before visual/command handling. That means pressing Ctrl-V while typing a command or chat inserts a raw control character into the buffer instead of only triggering block selection from command mode. Before this patch the byte was ignored outside handled control keys, and there is no regression test constraining Ctrl-V to visual block selection behavior.

review_fix_inputs.findings_section:
FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:816-818` and `src/ui_harness.rs:441-443` treat visual mode as plain command mode, so raw arrow keys dispatch `Esc` first and clear the visual selection before the parsed arrow is handled. Direct arrow keys are also consumed by the chat-arrow branches at `src/terminal_app.rs:588-602` / `src/ui_harness.rs:202-212`. The new visual arrow handling in `src/ui.rs:800-803` is therefore unreachable for the right pane, and tests only cover `h/j/k/l`.

- `src/ui.rs:1497-1510` clamps the block-selection cursor column to each target line length, then `src/ui.rs:1542-1551` applies the resulting min/max columns to every selected row. Moving a block selection from a long line onto a shorter line changes the rectangle width and can select extra earlier text; rows shorter than the block start are also dropped from yank output by `selection_text` at `src/ui.rs:1580-1585`. This needs uneven-line block-selection coverage.

FINDINGS

- `src/terminal_app.rs:1075-1082` maps raw Ctrl-V to `TerminalAppInput::Char(CTRL_V_CHAR)` for every mode, and the prompt/insert branches at `src/terminal_app.rs:560-568` push any `Char` directly into the command or chat buffer before the UI command handler can restrict Ctrl-V to visual-block mode. The same path exists in the harness at `src/ui_harness.rs:581-589` and `src/ui_harness.rs:184-188`. This means pressing Ctrl-V while typing inserts a raw U+0016 control character into prompts/messages, a regression from the previous ignored-control behavior and not covered by the new visual-mode tests.
